sources_considered.why: Reports that Gamma, a VC-backed AI startup, reached $100M ARR and 70M users while profitable.
Replit CEO says Replit is gross margin positive. Context on whether services were 'entirely unsustainable'.
Reports Cursor's negative 23% gross margin. Partial support for subsidised growth at one leading company.
Paywalled preview only, so it cannot be cited.

receipt.public_excerpt: The San Francisco-based startup surpassed $100 million in annual recurring revenue while maintaining profitability for over two years.

evidence_items.explanation: Gamma is a VC-backed AI startup that grew fast while profitable. That contradicts a strict universal reading. It does not test the counterfactual for the hyped companies he has in mind.

evidence_items.locator: section on market, paragraph beginning 'Right now, that bet looks very smart'

receipt.public_excerpt: He also said that unlike many AI-powered coding companies, Replit is gross margin positive.

evidence_items.explanation: Replit, one of the companies he names elsewhere, says it is gross margin positive. That cuts against 'entirely unsustainable', but it is the CEO's unaudited claim. The same line notes many competitors are not.

receipt.public_excerpt: Unlike Cursor, which he said has been operating at negative 23% gross margins, he argued Replit has the economics to make that path viable

evidence_items.explanation: Reports that Cursor, the fastest-growing example, ran negative gross margins. That fits his story for that company, but the source is a competitor citing press reports.

unresolved_gaps: No public data shows whether the leading fast-growing startups would have grown without subsidised pricing. That is the counterfactual 'only' requires.
Most startups do not publish audited margins or burn, so a claim about the whole population cannot be measured.
Whether one profitable fast-growing company like Gamma refutes a rhetorical generalisation depends on reading him as a strict universal.
